findings.description: Long-lived AWS access-key credentials are embedded in EC2 user data. User data is stored and can be retrieved by principals with instance-description access, while any compromise of the publicly reachable instance can expose and misuse these credentials.

The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so encryption relies on an account-level default that is not established in this configuration. Data written to this attached volume may therefore be stored unencrypted.
This snapshot is created from aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage, which is not configured for encryption. The snapshot will consequently preserve the volume's unencrypted state.
TCP/22 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0. The associated instance is in a public-IP subnet with a default route through an internet gateway, making SSH reachable from untrusted networks.
All outbound protocols and ports are allowed to 0.0.0.0/0. This removes egress network controls for the web host and allows unrestricted external connections following a compromise.
The bucket holding VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration. Flow-log records may be stored without an explicitly enforced encryption-at-rest control.
